review_items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed direct artifact f8fa8ddc6b3f46e89c9b1bd5a5482a49 against its accepted version-1 obligation/bindings, actual fixed Node harness and plan, and execution 0658bc3db0044fef9d8fa246d1dff118. No checker-correspondence issue found for the scoped Node interface admission discrepancy.

Requirement and interpretation: Node.ProposeConfChange explicitly says configuration changes are dropped unless the leader is certain there is no prior unapplied configuration. Node.Advance explicitly permits calling while application is ongoing; doc.go says any time after persistence, with application order preserved. The protobuf configuration contract says membership becomes active when applied. These jointly ground the local admission obligation for Node. RawNode.Advance has stronger completed-application wording, but the fixed driver never calls it directly: the public Node API owns the selected caller contract and internally delegates. Reading Node's permission as data-entry-only would require a configuration-specific restriction absent from the captured interface. This is a discrepancy with the contract as written, not evidence of intended maintainer policy or a universal safety theorem. The test does not rely on the separately disputed send-before-persistence permission: persistence is completed first throughout.

Prefix and caller duties: RestartNode initializes from an identical single-voter snapshot/HardState at index/term 1 and Applied=1. Actual Campaign and Ready/Advance create the initial leader entry, then ProposeConfChange creates and commits the first learner change at index 3. The driver applies only Ready.CommittedEntries and checks consecutive application indexes. It persists entries and HardState before every Advance; no runtime snapshot occurs. All remote traffic can be dropped because destinations are learners, not voters. The early-advance case retains the committed first Ready, calls public Advance, leaves ApplyConfChange pending, and submits the second change through Node. It later applies the held first entry before any newer entry and finishes all work at index 4. The permitted delayed application is finite; it is not an indefinitely withheld caller prerequisite used to manufacture nonprogress. The experiment concerns a synchronous admission decision completed while application is pending.

Timing and identity: before_second records first_index, scenario and the independently maintained userApplied before issuing the second proposal. That counter advances only after actual ApplyConfChange/ordered application; it is not derived from internal Status.Applied or the expected output. No concurrent application worker exists. The Node proposal channel receive and subsequent public Status call provide a serialization fence after proposal processing. In hold_advance, only after that fence does the driver apply the first configuration and Advance, so observing the second entry later does not confuse its earlier admission context. The result preserves the captured prior_applied_at_proposal. Identity (scenario,first_index) uniquely associates each second proposal with its actual preceding change; there is exactly one second proposal per case. Monitor correlations pair results 1,4,7 with prerequisites 0,3,6, with no parsing errors or missing result fields. The admission alias explicitly selects before_second. The second Ready is persisted and its actual Entry.Type is measured before remaining caller work is completed.

Oracle and observations: the property is the one-way implication prior_applied_at_proposal=false implies second_type!=EntryConfChange; it does not demand acceptance when application is complete. No comparison value is used as an identity filter or applicability condition. The fixed proposal type is legacy ConfChange, so EntryConfChange is the actual configuration-entry representation for this check. Hold control records userApplied=2, internal Applied=2, then second EntryNormal. Early Advance records userApplied=2, internal Applied=3, zero active learners, then second EntryConfChange at index 4 while userApplied remains 2 and learners remain zero. Apply-first control records userApplied=3 and one learner before the same second entry type is legitimately produced. Every history reaches completed with userApplied=4. Thus the result is a completed local eligibility comparison, not inferred from test success, proposal return value, timeout, or absent events.

Mechanism and limits: Node's Advance path delegates to RawNode.Advance, which processes the deferred storage-apply response and advances raftLog.applied even though the caller is using the advertised application overlap. stepLeader's pendingConfIndex > applied guard then no longer sees the first unapplied configuration. Actual active membership has not changed, independently shown by Status.Config and absence of ApplyConfChange. Withholding Advance or applying first preserves the intended boundary, as the controls show. No source mutation, fabricated message, canceled configuration or disabled validation is used. The two learner changes do not alter quorum requirements, and no conflicting decision or client outage is observed. Attribution is to this Node admission/API-contract mismatch, conditional on the explicit early-Advance permission, not to RawNode usage under a stronger completion contract.
limitations: Applicability is to the captured Node contract as written; an intended but undocumented configuration-specific early-Advance restriction is not established.
Single-voter learner changes measure local configuration admission, not quorum-change safety, conflicting commits, crashes or client-visible effects.
RawNode callers using its stronger completed-application interpretation and asynchronous-storage mode are outside the executed history.

feedback.answered: Initial A1/A2 connection: raft.appendEntry assigns the leader term and successive indexes and schedules a self MsgAppResp through send; send defers append and vote responses in msgsAfterAppend. maybeCommit combines the current term with tracker.Committed, but the tracker and log consumers still need inspection. Step generally rejects lower-term messages before role-specific dispatch. Current-term MsgStorageAppendResp may stabilize entries; lower-term completion does not stabilize entries but still applies a carried snapshot because that snapshot represents committed state. MsgStorageApplyResp carries term zero and records completed application independently of election term. RawNode Ready translates deferred replies into ordered storage responses in async mode; synchronous mode returns remote deferred replies in Ready.Messages and retains self replies for Advance. context.explanation: Election starts only for a promotable voter without unapplied committed configuration changes or pending snapshot. Vote grants require permitted prior-vote state and an up-to-date candidate log; current voter majorities aggregate votes, with self vote deferred to persistence. Reset clears old vote/progress/readOnly support and transfer state but retains committed log and pre-gate pending reads. Lower-term replies are rejected before role consumption; old storage append completion cannot trim entries but committed snapshot completion remains valid. connection.explanation: Authority is acquired with votes qualified by log history and local applied membership. Within that authority, durable append replies become eligible Match support for commit. Membership application changes which support is counted; outgoing voters remain required until joint exit, and learners do not count. Old volatile tallies are reset on authority transition, while committed history and term-independent application survive. Storage completions have separate generation checks before unstable history is discarded. Recovery reconstructs term/vote, committed history and configuration from caller storage rather than old volatile tallies. Read-index consumes both a current-term commitment gate and renewed quorum authority (except singleton/lease variants), with request identity and final read execution left to the caller. Node serialization and Ready ordering connect these mechanisms without making emitted work equivalent to completed external work.

Reviewed fixed artifact 4b82b66fa96f4bc3b93a10833dc75da1, its accepted claim/binding version 1, actual harness and plan, execution 97aac198d2bc4b10be4e3104e70bb614 and correlated monitor results. No correspondence issue found for the measured automatic-continuation proposition.

Applicability: JointImplicit assigns the zero-change proposal to Raft, whereas JointExplicit assigns it to the application. AutoLeave says to transition when possible. In the witnessed state node 1 remains an eligible leader, the implicit change is committed/applied, no transfer remains, and nodes 1 and 2 are a majority of both voter sets. The ordinary-proposal loss contract does not make unrelated client traffic a prerequisite of Raft-owned automatic work. No numeric deadline is inferred.

Legal entry and history: all nodes start from the same explicit configuration snapshot at index/term 1, with matching HardState and Applied=1, supported by NewRawNode's bootstrap guidance. The three actual RawNodes generate votes, entries and acknowledgments; the driver neither writes raft state nor forges support. It calls TransferLeader(3) serially during the leader's accepted Ready after the configuration entry has actually appeared in CommittedEntries and before ApplyConfChange/Advance. Ready/Advance does not prohibit serialized transfer while Ready is outstanding. The driver persists entries and HardState before any returned messages, applies only committed configuration entries in order and completes Advance after application. Voter 3 becomes unavailable at this point, with its traffic discarded; voter 2 and leader 1 continue ticking and processing every generated message and Ready. Learner 4 is absent in both control and transfer histories and is not required for either voter quorum. MemoryStorage substitutes completed durability, not protocol logic; no restart or physical durability claim follows.

Observation and identity: the prerequisite joint_committed is emitted for the actual entry before application; result fields and full retained state show that same entry subsequently applied. Identity is (scenario,joint_index), independent of the compared boolean, with admission Alias admitted. Monitor records match control result event 4 to prerequisite 0 and transfer result 10 to prerequisite 6. Both final result events are emitted regardless of stranded_cycle. The retained parsing_errors list is empty. Go's JSON output splits long state lines into chunks; reconstructing Output per test yielded complete CA_EVENT records and verified the fields rather than treating each chunk as a complete event.

Measured comparison: transfer admission is index 3, term 2, target 3. After application last=commit=applied=3, AutoLeave=true, outgoing count 3, no exit entry. At tick 10 target becomes 0. At ticks 20 and 30 full observed RawNode state repeats, work is drained, and ten actual heartbeat responses from voter 2 were consumed. Result stranded_cycle=true violates the independently stated no-stranded-automatic-work expectation. Control has exit index 4 applied, AutoLeave=false and stranded_cycle=false under the same unavailable-node fault. A later ordinary proposal occurs strictly after cycle_result and leads to exit index 5; it is recovery counterevidence, not an admission condition or a hidden completion substitute.

Recurrence correspondence: reflection recursively includes all scalar/collection protocol state in RawNode, raft, raftLog, unstable, readOnly, tracker including private sentCommit/inflight fields, and MemoryStorage entries/HardState/snapshot. It distinguishes nil and nonnil collections and compares canonical JSON strings without a hash. Function pointers tick/step are omitted, but the fixed source sets them from role transitions; the repeated role/term and the observed heartbeat-only paths do not change them. Log sinks and storage callStats do not choose protocol branches. Randomized election timeout values are included; global randomness is used only by resetRandomizedElectionTimeout, and the repeated leader/quorum and per-tick follower heartbeat path invokes no reset or election. The live queue is empty at both endpoints, storage/application work is drained, and the external scheduling rule repeats node 1 Tick, node 2 Tick and pump, with the unavailable-node policy fixed. Slice capacity and pointer alias identity are not serialized, but this cycle only produces/consumes heartbeat messages and does not mutate retained entries or membership, so these cannot enable a delayed exit. Driver diagnostic counters and loop index do not feed protocol calls within the repeated interval. Thus the ten-tick transition can recur under the same permitted live-quorum schedule; this is a finite recurring-state witness with sourced continuation, not a claim that thirty ticks alone proves eventual failure.

Cause and alternatives: appliedTo submits auto-exit but stepLeader drops it while leadTransferee is set. tickHeartbeat clears transfer without calling appliedTo or scheduling equivalent exit work. In the observed drained cycle no new committed application callback exists: leader beats only send heartbeats, follower heartbeats only commit the unchanged bounded index and respond, and leader responses refresh activity without appending new log work. A successful transfer, reelection or unrelated proposal can provide another application event. They explain recovery paths but do not invalidate the stable continuing-leader cycle. The observation establishes this local automatic-exit continuation defect, not consensus safety loss or a global client endpoint. A nonrecurring run would not prove general liveness; that limitation does not erase this complete recurring witness.

formation.explanation: A leader assigns its term and next index to admitted proposals and sends append requests. Followers match predecessor term/index, preserve committed entries, replace conflicting uncommitted suffixes and report append support after caller persistence. Leader dispatch admits term-qualified tracked responses, updates Match, aggregates only current voters (both majorities when joint), and advances commit only when the selected index has the current leader term. Append-response advancement releases postponed reads and broadcasts decisions; configuration-driven advancement separately broadcasts without that release call. Heartbeats carry a commit capped by peer Match. Followers propagate commit into Ready application delivery, whose external completion is caller-owned.

context.explanation: Election starts only for a promotable voter without unapplied committed configuration changes or pending snapshot. Vote grants require permitted prior-vote state and an up-to-date candidate log; current voter majorities aggregate votes, with self vote deferred to persistence. Pre-vote preserves term/vote and successful pre-vote starts the real campaign. Winning election resets progress, installs leader role and appends a current-term empty entry. Higher terms usually force follower role, with explicit pre-vote and lease exceptions. Reset clears old vote/progress/readOnly support and transfer state but retains committed log and pre-gate pending reads. Lower-term replies are rejected before role consumption; old storage append completion cannot trim entries but committed snapshot completion remains valid. Quorum loss can remove leadership, and transfer catches up a voter then asks it to campaign, abandoning unfinished transfer on timeout.

connection.explanation: Authority is acquired with votes qualified by log history and local applied membership. Within that authority, durable append replies become eligible Match support for commit. Membership application changes which support is counted; outgoing voters remain required until joint exit, and learners do not count. Old volatile tallies are reset on authority transition, while committed history and term-independent application survive. Storage completions have separate generation checks before unstable history is discarded. Recovery reconstructs term/vote, committed history and configuration from caller storage rather than old volatile tallies. Read-index consumes both a current-term commitment gate and renewed quorum authority (except singleton/lease variants), with request identity and final read execution left to the caller. Node serialization and Ready ordering connect these mechanisms without making emitted work equivalent to completed external work.

Reviewed fixed artifact 4b82b66fa96f4bc3b93a10833dc75da1, its accepted claim/binding version 1, actual harness and plan, execution 97aac198d2bc4b10be4e3104e70bb614 and correlated monitor results. No correspondence issue found for the measured automatic-continuation proposition.

Applicability: JointImplicit assigns the zero-change proposal to Raft, whereas JointExplicit assigns it to the application. AutoLeave says to transition when possible. In the witnessed state node 1 remains an eligible leader, the implicit change is committed/applied, no transfer remains, and nodes 1 and 2 are a majority of both voter sets. The ordinary-proposal loss contract does not make unrelated client traffic a prerequisite of Raft-owned automatic work. No numeric deadline is inferred.

Legal entry and history: all nodes start from the same explicit configuration snapshot at index/term 1, with matching HardState and Applied=1, supported by NewRawNode's bootstrap guidance. The three actual RawNodes generate votes, entries and acknowledgments; the driver neither writes raft state nor forges support. It calls TransferLeader(3) serially during the leader's accepted Ready after the configuration entry has actually appeared in CommittedEntries and before ApplyConfChange/Advance. Ready/Advance does not prohibit serialized transfer while Ready is outstanding. The driver persists entries and HardState before any returned messages, applies only committed configuration entries in order and completes Advance after application. Voter 3 becomes unavailable at this point, with its traffic discarded; voter 2 and leader 1 continue ticking and processing every generated message and Ready. Learner 4 is absent in both control and transfer histories and is not required for either voter quorum. MemoryStorage substitutes completed durability, not protocol logic; no restart or physical durability claim follows.

Observation and identity: the prerequisite joint_committed is emitted for the actual entry before application; result fields and full retained state show that same entry subsequently applied. Identity is (scenario,joint_index), independent of the compared boolean, with admission Alias admitted. Monitor records match control result event 4 to prerequisite 0 and transfer result 10 to prerequisite 6. Both final result events are emitted regardless of stranded_cycle. The retained parsing_errors list is empty. Go's JSON output splits long state lines into chunks; reconstructing Output per test yielded complete CA_EVENT records and verified the fields rather than treating each chunk as a complete event.

Measured comparison: transfer admission is index 3, term 2, target 3. After application last=commit=applied=3, AutoLeave=true, outgoing count 3, no exit entry. At tick 10 target becomes 0. At ticks 20 and 30 full observed RawNode state repeats, work is drained, and ten actual heartbeat responses from voter 2 were consumed. Result stranded_cycle=true violates the independently stated no-stranded-automatic-work expectation. Control has exit index 4 applied, AutoLeave=false and stranded_cycle=false under the same unavailable-node fault. A later ordinary proposal occurs strictly after cycle_result and leads to exit index 5; it is recovery counterevidence, not an admission condition or a hidden completion substitute.

Recurrence correspondence: reflection recursively includes all scalar/collection protocol state in RawNode, raft, raftLog, unstable, readOnly, tracker including private sentCommit/inflight fields, and MemoryStorage entries/HardState/snapshot. It distinguishes nil and nonnil collections and compares canonical JSON strings without a hash. Function pointers tick/step are omitted, but the fixed source sets them from role transitions; the repeated role/term and the observed heartbeat-only paths do not change them. Log sinks and storage callStats do not choose protocol branches. Randomized election timeout values are included; global randomness is used only by resetRandomizedElectionTimeout, and the repeated leader/quorum and per-tick follower heartbeat path invokes no reset or election. The live queue is empty at both endpoints, storage/application work is drained, and the external scheduling rule repeats node 1 Tick, node 2 Tick and pump, with the unavailable-node policy fixed. Slice capacity and pointer alias identity are not serialized, but this cycle only produces/consumes heartbeat messages and does not mutate retained entries or membership, so these cannot enable a delayed exit. Driver diagnostic counters and loop index do not feed protocol calls within the repeated interval. Thus the ten-tick transition can recur under the same permitted live-quorum schedule; this is a finite recurring-state witness with sourced continuation, not a claim that thirty ticks alone proves eventual failure.

Cause and alternatives: appliedTo submits auto-exit but stepLeader drops it while leadTransferee is set. tickHeartbeat clears transfer without calling appliedTo or scheduling equivalent exit work. In the observed drained cycle no new committed application callback exists: leader beats only send heartbeats, follower heartbeats only commit the unchanged bounded index and respond, and leader responses refresh activity without appending new log work. A successful transfer, reelection or unrelated proposal can provide another application event. They explain recovery paths but do not invalidate the stable continuing-leader cycle. The observation establishes this local automatic-exit continuation defect, not consensus safety loss or a global client endpoint. A nonrecurring run would not prove general liveness; that limitation does not erase this complete recurring witness.

items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed direct artifact f8fa8ddc6b3f46e89c9b1bd5a5482a49 against its accepted version-1 obligation/bindings, actual fixed Node harness and plan, and execution 0658bc3db0044fef9d8fa246d1dff118. No checker-correspondence issue found for the scoped Node interface admission discrepancy.

Requirement and interpretation: Node.ProposeConfChange explicitly says configuration changes are dropped unless the leader is certain there is no prior unapplied configuration. Node.Advance explicitly permits calling while application is ongoing; doc.go says any time after persistence, with application order preserved. The protobuf configuration contract says membership becomes active when applied. These jointly ground the local admission obligation for Node. RawNode.Advance has stronger completed-application wording, but the fixed driver never calls it directly: the public Node API owns the selected caller contract and internally delegates. Reading Node's permission as data-entry-only would require a configuration-specific restriction absent from the captured interface. This is a discrepancy with the contract as written, not evidence of intended maintainer policy or a universal safety theorem. The test does not rely on the separately disputed send-before-persistence permission: persistence is completed first throughout.

Prefix and caller duties: RestartNode initializes from an identical single-voter snapshot/HardState at index/term 1 and Applied=1. Actual Campaign and Ready/Advance create the initial leader entry, then ProposeConfChange creates and commits the first learner change at index 3. The driver applies only Ready.CommittedEntries and checks consecutive application indexes. It persists entries and HardState before every Advance; no runtime snapshot occurs. All remote traffic can be dropped because destinations are learners, not voters. The early-advance case retains the committed first Ready, calls public Advance, leaves ApplyConfChange pending, and submits the second change through Node. It later applies the held first entry before any newer entry and finishes all work at index 4. The permitted delayed application is finite; it is not an indefinitely withheld caller prerequisite used to manufacture nonprogress. The experiment concerns a synchronous admission decision completed while application is pending.

Timing and identity: before_second records first_index, scenario and the independently maintained userApplied before issuing the second proposal. That counter advances only after actual ApplyConfChange/ordered application; it is not derived from internal Status.Applied or the expected output. No concurrent application worker exists. The Node proposal channel receive and subsequent public Status call provide a serialization fence after proposal processing. In hold_advance, only after that fence does the driver apply the first configuration and Advance, so observing the second entry later does not confuse its earlier admission context. The result preserves the captured prior_applied_at_proposal. Identity (scenario,first_index) uniquely associates each second proposal with its actual preceding change; there is exactly one second proposal per case. Monitor correlations pair results 1,4,7 with prerequisites 0,3,6, with no parsing errors or missing result fields. The admission alias explicitly selects before_second. The second Ready is persisted and its actual Entry.Type is measured before remaining caller work is completed.

Oracle and observations: the property is the one-way implication prior_applied_at_proposal=false implies second_type!=EntryConfChange; it does not demand acceptance when application is complete. No comparison value is used as an identity filter or applicability condition. The fixed proposal type is legacy ConfChange, so EntryConfChange is the actual configuration-entry representation for this check. Hold control records userApplied=2, internal Applied=2, then second EntryNormal. Early Advance records userApplied=2, internal Applied=3, zero active learners, then second EntryConfChange at index 4 while userApplied remains 2 and learners remain zero. Apply-first control records userApplied=3 and one learner before the same second entry type is legitimately produced. Every history reaches completed with userApplied=4. Thus the result is a completed local eligibility comparison, not inferred from test success, proposal return value, timeout, or absent events.

Mechanism and limits: Node's Advance path delegates to RawNode.Advance, which processes the deferred storage-apply response and advances raftLog.applied even though the caller is using the advertised application overlap. stepLeader's pendingConfIndex > applied guard then no longer sees the first unapplied configuration. Actual active membership has not changed, independently shown by Status.Config and absence of ApplyConfChange. Withholding Advance or applying first preserves the intended boundary, as the controls show. No source mutation, fabricated message, canceled configuration or disabled validation is used. The two learner changes do not alter quorum requirements, and no conflicting decision or client outage is observed. Attribution is to this Node admission/API-contract mismatch, conditional on the explicit early-Advance permission, not to RawNode usage under a stronger completion contract.
